President Biden ran for office to restore the soul of our nation – and he has been clear that hate, bigotry, and violence have no place here in the U.S. 
 
That’s why our Administration has taken numerous steps to counter hate in all its forms. In 2021, President Biden signed into law the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act, which includes the Khalid Jabara and Heather Heyer NO HATE Act, to improve the reporting and prevention of hate crimes and ensure that hate crimes information is more accessible to Asian American and Pacific Islander Communities. Attorney General Merrick Garland also appointed the Justice Department’s first-ever Anti-Hate Crimes Resources Coordinator and designated staff to oversee expedited review of hate crimes. And, the Federal Bureau of Investigation has elevated hate crimes and criminal civil rights violations to its highest-level national threat priority.
 
In 2022, President Biden hosted the first-ever White House United We Stand Summit to address hate-fueled violence and put forward a shared vision for working toward a more united America. At the Summit, President Biden announced the White House Initiative to Counter Hate-Motivated Violence to address violence and bias against all communities.
 
President Biden also established an interagency group to increase and better coordinate federal efforts to counter Antisemitism, Islamophobia, and related forms of bias and discrimination within the U.S. In 2023, amidst a historic increase in antisemitic incidents, President Biden released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism. In 2024, he released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Islamophobia and Anti-Arab Hate.
 
The power is within each of us to rise together against hate and build a nation that treats everyone with dignity and respect.

President Biden believes that artificial intelligence is one of the most powerful tools of our time – but knows that to seize its opportunities, we must first mitigate its risks.

In 2023, President Biden issued a sweeping Executive Order on AI to ensure that America leads the way toward responsible AI innovation. The Executive Order takes a comprehensive approach to America’s global leadership in AI, encourages responsible innovation, and promotes competition. It also ensures that as new technologies rapidly evolve, the government continues to protect Americans’ privacy, advance equity and civil rights, and stand up for consumers, patients, students, and workers.

Additionally, thanks to President Biden’s leadership, 16 companies have made voluntary commitments on safe and responsible AI use. These commitments include internal and external security testing before releasing AI systems, sharing information with the public about safety risks and dangerous capabilities, and deploying AI to help address society’s greatest challenges.

Our Administration took critical steps to achieve this decrease – including seizing more fentanyl at the border, arresting and prosecuting dozens of high-level drug traffickers and cartel leaders, sanctioning over 300 entities and individuals involved in the global illicit drug trade, and forging historic counternarcotics cooperation with China.

Our Administration also expanded access to naloxone and other life-saving interventions, including working with Congress to remove barriers that prevented medical professionals from prescribing treatment for opioid use disorder.

Junk fees are hidden or unfair costs that too many companies – airlines, banks, hotels, ticket sellers – charge consumers. These fees may not matter to the very wealthy, but they add up and take real money out of the pockets of working families.

That’s why our Administration has been working to ban these fees and save families hundreds of dollars each year. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau took action to lower overdraft and credit card late fees, the Department of Transportation proposed a ban on family seating fees and required upfront disclosure of baggage and change fees, the Federal Communications Commission ensured consumers see upfront the full price and terms for their internet service, and the Federal Trade Commission banned hidden junk fees for live-event tickets and hotel bookings.

Collectively, the Biden-Harris Administration’s actions to cut junk fees will save Americans more than $20 billion a year. We were tired of the American people being played for suckers, and we took action.

President Biden believes no one should be jailed just for using or possessing marijuana. To help remedy our nation’s failed approach to marijuana, President Biden pardoned federal and D.C. simple marijuana possession offenses. President Biden also called on governors to issue similar pardons for state offenses. And, President Biden requested that the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services review how marijuana is scheduled under federal law.

In May 2024, the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services began the process to reschedule marijuana from a Schedule I to a Schedule III drug under federal law. Following the President’s lead, governors in Maryland, Massachusetts, and Oregon also issued pardons for some marijuana state offenses.

Far too many lives have been upended because of our nation’s failed approach to marijuana. President Biden took action to right those historic wrongs.

- Efforts to surge food, water, and other commodities continue in areas of Western North Carolina

Combats Emerging Firearm Threats
- The new Emerging Firearms Threats Task Force will combat the emerging threats of machinegun conversion devices and unserialized, 3D-printed firearms. Within 90 days, the Task Force will send President Biden a risk assessment and a strategy to address these threats.

tweets.text:
Today, President Biden spoke with four individuals from across the country about how our Administration’s Investing in America agenda is benefitting their lives and planting the seeds for a brighter future for their community.
 
Here are their stories:

Mayor Woodfin from Birmingham, Alabama highlighted several projects from President Biden and Vice President Harris’s Investing in America agenda that are growing the economy and creating opportunities for Birmingham families and communities.

Jackie is a retired schoolteacher living in Muskego, Wisconsin, with her husband Doug. She has an incurable but treatable blood cancer and takes the blood thinner Xarelto, which was one of the first ten drugs Medicare negotiated a lower price for in the first year of the program. With her current Medicare insurance, Jackie’s prescription drugs can cost her tens of thousands of dollars in out-of-pocket costs per year. Because of the Biden-Harris Administration’s Inflation Reduction Act, Jackie’s out of pocket prescription drug costs will be capped at $2,000 starting next year. Jackie spoke with President Biden about how his actions to lower prescription drug costs will give her and her family breathing room in their daily lives.

Chairwoman Flores of the Colorado River Indian Tribes highlighted infrastructure investments from President Biden and Vice President Harris’s Investing in America agenda that are delivering clean water and creating more opportunity for families and the Colorado River Indian Tribes community.

Cecilia is a Philadelphia Chinatown resident. She was a widow and single mother when she learned that her community church and the school, Holy Redeemer, would be demolished for a federal highway project. Later her home would be taken via eminent domain for the Center City Commuter Rail Tunnel. She and hundreds of residents were eventually displaced, but Cecilia went on to help form the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation, a nonprofit that helped develop housing for low-income Philadelphians, seniors, and help small business owners. She never gave up on her dream of capping the dangerous Vine Street Expressway. Thanks to President Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act and the Reconnecting Communities program, her dream will come true.

Our Administration will continue to deliver direct results in communities across the country.

Cecilia is a Philadelphia Chinatown resident. She was a widow and single mother when she learned that her community church and the school, Holy Redeemer, would be demolished for a federal highway project. Later her home would be taken via eminent domain for the Center City Commuter Rail Tunnel. She and hundreds of residents were eventually displaced, but Cecilia went on to help form the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation, a nonprofit that helped develop housing for low-income Philadelphians, seniors, and help small business owners.
